# Source checkpoint history

v1 is superseded before any candidate execution. Its initial-recognition collector recorded literal false rather than reading the actual constructed parser. Its parse-attempt field was a wrapper branch count rather than a real parser-entry-hook counter. v2 reads the actual constructor bit and counts actual full-parser entries. It also captures before/after recognition state around the original assignment and records only actual false-to-true transitions. The direct path-segment seam reports the actual constructed initial bit but has zero full-parser entries and no final recognition observation.

The earlier v4 derived build failed due to an observer format-string brace. v5 corrected that compile-only defect and built successfully. These logs remain separate; v5 is not the final v2 source package and no qualifying run uses its identity.

Other v2 signals were checked for the same blind spot: node counts use the actual parser ledger, allocator counts/traces use the real allocator, field scan spans/indices and source/work/append/reserve deltas use real hooks, full AST/provenance use the actual returned Program, diagnostics use actual renderers, token inventory uses admitted tokens, and runtime OS/architecture/width come from the executable. Canonical AST normalization supplies no expected values.

Independent review superseded v2 before candidate execution because it copied the next_kind iterator into a field-specific helper. v3 instead brackets a call to the original next_kind method, and adds a passive inspect callback to that original iterator. The callback obtains actual token indices from safe address arithmetic within the same token tape, checks kind/span against the admitted tape, and records them only while the field scope is active. Hidden helper reads, reserve/appends or namespace work are therefore observed within the real operation.

v3 exact compilation found a missing format-string escape brace in the newly observed after-bit JSON field. v4 adds only that brace to observer logic; source instrumentation is unchanged. Both instrumented/control v3 compile logs remain retained. No v3 candidate runtime executed.

v5 adds a non-assert import-time rejection of optimized Python to prepare/build/run/passivity before argument parsing, output creation or subprocess work. The mechanical Debug decoder was audited and left unchanged: it uses explicit exceptions and contains no assert-based admission gates. A real subprocess control executes each helper with both -O and PYTHONOPTIMIZE=1, requires the specific rejection, records raw stdout/stderr and checks destination absence plus a test-only subprocess-invocation sentinel. Rust observer and instrumentation bytes are unchanged; existing normal-run build/passivity receipts retain their historical v4 helper identities and need an explicit helper-only rebind rather than rewriting.

v6 fixes a platform-observation labeling gap before any frozen-corpus execution. Rust std::env::consts OS/ARCH describe the compiled process target, so the collection driver now separately measures platform.uname and native Python pointer size, preserves that evidence in the execution manifest, rejects unsupported host/target tuples before output/execution, and requires measured host agreement with raw process ABI values. Actual-runtime binding fields use this measured host. Rust/binary bytes remain unchanged. A synthetic mismatch control rejects an aarch64 measured host for an x86_64 raw process.

The first unsupported-host process-control attempt used platform.uname._replace, which forces Python's lazy processor probe and hit the subprocess sentinel during import. That harness-only failed attempt is preserved separately and is not passing evidence. The corrected controls use explicit measured-field substitutions without forcing processor lookup; all three unsupported OS/machine/width cases now reject by the named platform gate with no destination or candidate invocation.

v7 removes quadratic suffix copying from the mechanical Debug decoder. Only three unanchored regex matches change to precompiled Pattern.match on the original string at the same cursor; len(match[0]) cursor increments and all error paths remain unchanged. Seventy-five old/new string, escape, nested and invalid-input controls match outputs or exception type/arguments. The complete retained v6 result for the100,000-token trivia case exactly equals the new decode of its8,944,765-byte Debug text, which took2.03s in the recorded control. The original full-v6-debug run completed248cases/319rows and remains intact. Rust, compiler behavior, normalized schema and frozen expectations are unchanged; new collection requires an explicit reviewed helper rebind.
